As soon as she got home, she informed her parents that she had accepted the only true
faith and that she would therefore have to leave them and make her home at the Ingmar
Her parents asked her, of course, why she wanted to leave home.
So she'd be able to lead a righteous life, she up and told them.
But they seemed to think that could be done just as effectively at home with them.
Oh, no, that wouldn't be possible, she declared, unless one could live with those who were
Her father then asked her if all of them were going to live on the Ingmar farm.
The others had true Christians in their own homes.
Now Clementson is a pretty good sort, as you know, and both he and his wife tried to reason
with Gunhild in all kindness, but she stood firm.
At last, her father became so exasperated that he just took her and locked her up in
her room, telling her she'd have to stay there till this crazy fit had passed.
